highlights.description: Anthropic opened its virtual "Briefing: Enterprise Agents" event on Tuesday with a provocation. highlights.title: Canada Wants OpenAI to Present Safety Plan After Shooter’s ChatGPT Use
highlights.description: The Canadian government says it expects OpenAI Inc. to present “concrete” safety steps after the company opted not to inform police about a teenager from British Columbia who’d played out violent scenarios on ChatGPT.

highlights.title: Anthropic just released a mobile version of Claude Code called Remote Control
highlights.description: Claude Code has become increasingly popular in the first year since its launch, and especially in recent months, as developers and non-technical users alike flock to AI unicorn Anthropic's hit coding agent to create full applications and websites in days, on their own, that would've taken months and technical teams without. highlights.title: Anthropic Adds Caveat to AI Safety Policy in Race Against Rivals
highlights.description: Anthropic PBC, known for its commitment to artificial intelligence safeguards, has loosened its central safety policy, saying the change is necessary to remain competitive.

highlights.title: Nvidia challenger AI chip startup MatX raised $500M
highlights.description: The startup was founded by former Google TPU engineers in 2023.

highlights.title: Floodgates open for Tesla lawsuits, Waymo expands, and US goes nuclear
highlights.description: On today’s high-dollar episode of Quick Charge, Tesla is reeling from a $243 million judgement against it in a high-profile wrongful death case involving the company’s Autopilot system, and has a hard time getting the relevant data to NHTSA. more…

highlights.title: Wayve CEO on Robotaxis, Automaker Partnerships, Software
highlights.description: Wayve Ltd. CEO Alex Kendall discusses the UK self-driving company’s global autonomy platform, its partnerships with Nissan, Mercedes and Stellantis, and plans for mass production of robotaxis. He also talks about high-margin software business with some of the world’s largest OEMs, saying, “we’re excited to see our technology go head-to-head.” Kendall speaks with Bloomberg’s Tom Mackenzie in London. (Source: Bloomberg)
